notes: Gurobi reports ObjVal 37.323210208464126, status optimal, MIP gap 0 (solved at the root), NumVars 966 (7 x + 476 y + 7 V + 476 nu), NumConstrs 1987 (476 select + 1 drone_limit + 68 ohca + 7 stability + 7 aux0 + 3 x 476 aux1-3), NumIntVars 483 (all binary). The notebook has one model; it is the instance the notebook builds: incidents with ReceivedTime between '2019-05-31' and '2019-06-30' as strings (69 OHCAs at 68 locations, so 30 Jun itself is excluded; n_days = 30) and bases with ID 2, 3, 5, 14, 25, 31, 35. Optimum opens 21 MUNICIPAL CTR Fire Station, 800 VIRGINIA BEACH BLVD Fire Station, 3769 E. STRATFORD ROAD Rescue Squad and 5145 RURITAN COURT Rescue Squad (12/16/4/36 locations). Uniqueness: a no-good cut on the assignment gives 37.34427 and a no-good cut on the base set 38.31289, so the plan and every KPI are unique; SCORING_KPIS = response_objective, bases_opened, avg_wait_minutes, avg_flight_minutes, max_base_utilization. Notebook quirk reproduced: the objective's travel term is arrival_rate * distance / speed with distance in meters and speed in km/h (1000x hours), while service_time uses 0.001 * distance; the objective is therefore in mixed units and dominated by flight distance. KPIs report wait and flight in true minutes. (The markdown writes V_j with s*y in its second sum; the code uses s*nu, which is the correct linearisation of V_j = sum lambda s^2 y / (1 - rho_j); the port follows the code.) Data: incidents.csv is the per-location count in the notebook window (rate = round(incidents / (24 * observation_days), 6), the 6-decimal rounding of the original kept as a structural step), distances.csv is the Haversine column for the 476 pairs, bases.csv the 7 bases named Street + Type as in the notebook; n_drones, speed, maintenance and n_days are params. Vbar = 2 * sum of service times over all pairs is a structural big-M (not data). Same formulation, no reformulation.
